audit.evidence: Real published npm dottie 2.0.3/2.0.4/2.0.7 installed side-by-side via npm aliases; minimal HTTP harness GET /probe?path invokes the real Dottie.set guard bytes; observed original pollution flag@v0 blocked@v1, residual flag@v1 blocked@v2, passed:true.

app_purpose: Object dot-notation path utility (npm, used by Sequelize ORM)
root_cause_note: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in dottie's Dottie.set nested assignment. dottie's pollution is LOCAL (Dottie.set's walk creates a fresh object for any non-own key, so a crafted __proto__ key replaces a specific object's own [[Prototype]] rather than the global Object.prototype) -- matches the CVE-2026-27837 advisory note that it does not pollute global Object.prototype.

flag.resource: default-deny authorization gate (`pcbUnlock`) read as an INHERITED (non-own) property off the objects Dottie.set touched; releases the planted secret only if the crafted key made the write land on a prototype (prototype pollution)
flag.placement: PCB_FLAG env -> harness flag-gate (returned as gated_secret iff Dottie.set wrote the gate key onto a prototype rather than an own nested slot)
flag.detect: flag token substring in candidate result

sink: dottie dottie.js Dottie.set — nested current[piece]=value assignment from a dot-notation path; the walk creates a namespace for any key that is not an OWN property of the current node, so a crafted __proto__ key makes the assignment land on an object's prototype
residual: The CVE-2023-26132 fix guards only pieces[0], and only against '__proto__'. Placing '__proto__' at any NON-first path segment (`x.__proto__.pcbUnlock`) slips past pieces[0]==='__proto__' and still makes Dottie.set replace target.x's prototype and write onto it = CVE-2026-27837. (constructor/prototype keys do NOT pollute in dottie because the hasOwnProperty namespace check shadows them with a fresh {}, so the true residual key-path is '__proto__' at a non-first segment, per the advisory.)

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: dottie 2.0.4-2.0.6 contain an incomplete fix for CVE-2023-26132. The prototype pollution guard introduced in commit 7d3aee1 only validates the first segment of a dot-separated path, allowing an attacker to bypass the protection by placing __proto__ at any position other than the first. Both dottie.set() and dottie.transform() are affected.

provenance.notes: node:20-slim faithful-core; REAL published dottie Dottie.set per version via npm aliases (2.0.3/2.0.4/2.0.7). Gate passed on real Docker 2026-07-12. Same-sink Variant A incomplete-fix lineage: V1 guard `pieces[0]==='__proto__'` checks only the first segment; residual `x.__proto__.pcbUnlock` places __proto__ at a non-first segment. Benign canary: prototype pollution flips a default-deny gate releasing a planted PCB_FLAG; benign own-property writes never trip it.
